speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with a breast mass; to begin our assessment, have you noticed any changes in the size, shape, or hardness of this lump, and do you experience any pain or skin changes in the area?

speaker: Patient
text: 48-year-old woman. The patient noticed a mass in her left breast 4 weeks ago, which has rapidly increased in size. She denies any recent trauma or infections. No history of similar complaints in the past.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Given the rapid growth of this mass in just four weeks, have you noticed any skin changes like dimpling, redness, or warmth over the lump? Also, are there any swollen lymph nodes in your armpit?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Presence of a left breast mass. I also have Rapid increase in size of the mass, No skin or nipple changes, No pain associated with the mass. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Inflammatory Breast Cancer. The rapid growth of the mass over four weeks combined with the absence of skin changes (which would suggest abscess or mastitis) is highly atypical for benign conditions. Given the aggressive presentation and lack of pain, I suspect a high-grade malignancy. REQUEST TEST: Mammogram, Ultrasound, and Bilateral Axillary Ultrasound.
